title: Smooth-curve calculations
statement:
Let $k$ be an algebraically closed field of characteristic exponent $p$ ($p=\operatorname{char}k$ if $\operatorname{char}k>0$), let $C$ be a smooth separated connected curve over $k$ ([def-sc-curves]), let $r$ be a prime number, and let $\mathbf F_r=\underline{\mathbf Z/r\mathbf Z}$ be the constant etale sheaf on $C_{\Et}$ ([def-sc-constant-sheaves]). Then $(C,\mathbf F_r)$ is a curve coefficient pair and $\mathbf F_r$ is constructible ([def-weil-pbc-constructible-torsion]). Consider the assertions $\mathcal C_1(C,\mathbf F_r),\dots,\mathcal C_8(C,\mathbf F_r)$ of [def-weil-pbc-eight-curve-assertions], each read for the single pair $(C,\mathbf F_r)$ as an implication whose conclusion is asserted when its hypotheses (affine, proper, $p$-primary, constructible and prime to $p$) hold.

1. **(a)** If $r\neq\operatorname{char}k$ (every prime when $\operatorname{char}k=0$), then $\mathbf F_r$ satisfies $\mathcal C_1$, $\mathcal C_4$, $\mathcal C_6$ and $\mathcal C_8$; it satisfies $\mathcal C_2$ when $C$ is affine and $\mathcal C_5$, $\mathcal C_7$ when $C$ is proper. Explicitly, fix a primitive $r$-th root of unity $\zeta\in k$ and the trivialization $\theta_\zeta:\mathbf F_r\xrightarrow{\sim}\mu_r$ ([def-sc-mu-trivialization]). Then
$$
H^0(C_{\Et},\mathbf F_r)\cong\mathbf Z/r\mathbf Z,
$$
there is a short exact sequence
$$
0\longrightarrow\mathcal O_C(C)^\times/\mathcal O_C(C)^{\times r}
\longrightarrow H^1(C_{\Et},\mathbf F_r)
\longrightarrow\operatorname{Pic}(C)[r]\longrightarrow0
$$
($\operatorname{Pic}(C)$ as in [def-sc-picard-group]), and $H^2(C_{\Et},\mathbf F_r)=0$ if $C$ is affine. If $C$ is proper of genus $g$ ([def-sc-genus]),
$$
H^0(C_{\Et},\mathbf F_r)\cong\mathbf Z/r\mathbf Z,\quad
H^1(C_{\Et},\mathbf F_r)\cong(\mathbf Z/r\mathbf Z)^{2g},\quad
H^2(C_{\Et},\mathbf F_r)\cong\mathbf Z/r\mathbf Z,\quad
H^q(C_{\Et},\mathbf F_r)=0\ (q>2).
$$
These groups do not change under algebraically closed field extension: for every extension $k\subseteq k'$ of algebraically closed fields and every $q\ge0$ the pullback map $\rho^q_{k'/k}(C,\mathbf F_r):H^q(C_{\Et},\mathbf F_r)\to H^q((C_{k'})_{\Et},\mathbf F_r)$ of [def-sc-field-extension] is an isomorphism, and the pullback of $\theta_\zeta$ to $C_{k'}$ is $\theta_{\zeta'}$ for the image $\zeta'$ of $\zeta$ in $k'$, again a primitive $r$-th root of unity.
1. **(b)** If $\operatorname{char}k=p>0$ and $r=p$, then $\mathbf F_p$ satisfies $\mathcal C_1$, $\mathcal C_3$ and $\mathcal C_8$; it satisfies $\mathcal C_2$ when $C$ is affine and $\mathcal C_5$, $\mathcal C_7$ when $C$ is proper.
1. **(c)** The maps in $\mathcal C_6$, $\mathcal C_7$ and $\mathcal C_8$ for $(C,\mathbf F_r)$ are the pullback maps $\rho^q_{k'/k}(C,\mathbf F_r)$ of [def-weil-pbc-extension-pullback], which are those of [def-sc-field-extension], and the restriction maps $a^*:H^2(C_{\Et},\mathbf F_r)\to H^2(U_{\Et},a^{-1}\mathbf F_r)$ along open immersions $a:U\hookrightarrow C$, where $a^{-1}\mathbf F_r$ is the constant sheaf $\underline{\mathbf Z/r\mathbf Z}$ on $U_{\Et}$.
1. **(d)** Consequently, for every prime $r$, all eight assertions $\mathcal C(C,\mathbf F_r)$ of [def-weil-pbc-eight-curve-assertions] hold: in case (a) $\mathcal C_3$ holds vacuously ($\mathbf F_r$ is not $p$-primary, or $\operatorname{char}k=0$), in case (b) $\mathcal C_4$ and $\mathcal C_6$ hold vacuously ($\mathbf F_p$ is not prime to $p$), and $\mathcal C_2$, $\mathcal C_5$, $\mathcal C_7$ hold vacuously when their hypothesis on $C$ fails.

proof.text: Setting and coefficient conditions. By [def-sc-curves], $C$ is a separated scheme of finite type over $k$ of dimension one, so $\dim C\le1$. The constant sheaf $\mathbf F_r=\underline{\mathbf Z/r\mathbf Z}$ ([def-sc-constant-sheaves]) is killed by $r$ (multiplication by $r$ is zero on the constant presheaf, hence on its sheafification), so every local section is killed by the positive integer $r$ and $\mathbf F_r$ is torsion ([def-weil-pbc-etale-sheaves]); thus $(C,\mathbf F_r)$ is a curve coefficient pair ([def-weil-pbc-curve-setting]). It is constructible ([def-weil-pbc-constructible-torsion]): take the partition of $C$ into the single stratum $C$ (locally closed and constructible), on which $\mathbf F_r$ is constant, hence locally constant, with finite stalks $\mathbf Z/r\mathbf Z$. Its geometric stalks are $\mathbf Z/r\mathbf Z$ ([def-sc-constant-sheaves]), so by [def-weil-pbc-primary-torsion]: if $r\neq\operatorname{char}k$, every stalk element has order dividing the prime $r$, coprime to $p$, so $\mathbf F_r$ is prime to $p$ (no condition in characteristic $0$), and it is not $p$-primary (the class of $1$ has order $r$, not a power of $p$); if $r=p=\operatorname{char}k>0$, every stalk element is killed by $p$, so $\mathbf F_p$ is $p$-primary, and it is not prime to $p$ (the class of $1$ has order $p$).

source.place: Situation 0A52 (Tag 0A52) and the statement of Lemma 0A5B (Tag 0A5B): F = Z/lZ on a smooth X

proof.text: The maps (part (c)). For the pair $(C,\mathbf F_r)$ and an algebraically closed extension $k'/k$, [def-weil-pbc-extension-pullback] and [def-sc-field-extension] define the same map: both take $\pi_{k'}:C_{k'}=C\times_kk'\to C$, $F_{k'}=\pi_{k'}^{-1}\mathbf F_r$, and the pullback map $H^q(C_{\Et},\mathbf F_r)\to H^q((C_{k'})_{\Et},F_{k'})$ in degree $q$; and $\pi_{k'}^{-1}\mathbf F_r$ is the constant sheaf $\underline{\mathbf Z/r\mathbf Z}$ on $C_{k'}$, because inverse image ([def-weil-pbc-inverse-image]) is the sheafification of the presheaf inverse image, and the presheaf inverse image of a constant presheaf is the constant presheaf with the same value, so by left adjointness the sheafified pullback of the constant sheaf is the constant sheaf. This is the map of $\mathcal C_6$ and $\mathcal C_7$ ([def-weil-pbc-C6], [def-weil-pbc-C7]) and the map $\rho^q_{k'/k}(C,\mathbf F_r)$ in [lem-sc-c6] and [lem-sc-c7]. For an open immersion $a:U\hookrightarrow C$, likewise $a^{-1}\mathbf F_r$ is the constant sheaf $\underline{\mathbf Z/r\mathbf Z}$ on $U_{\Et}$, so the map $a^*:H^2(C_{\Et},\mathbf F_r)\to H^2(U_{\Et},a^{-1}\mathbf F_r)$ of $\mathcal C_8$ ([def-weil-pbc-C8]) is the restriction map $H^2(C_{\Et},\mathbf F_r)\to H^2(U_{\Et},\mathbf F_r)$ of [lem-sc-c8]. Hence the conclusions of [lem-sc-c6], [lem-sc-c7], [lem-sc-c8] are literally the conclusions of $\mathcal C_6$, $\mathcal C_7$, $\mathcal C_8$ for $(C,\mathbf F_r)$, as listed in [def-weil-pbc-eight-curve-assertions].

proof.text: Part (a), unconditional assertions ($r\neq\operatorname{char}k$). The hypotheses of [lem-sc-c1] ($k$ algebraically closed, $C$ smooth separated connected, $n=r$ prime) hold, so $H^q(C_{\Et},\mathbf F_r)=0$ for $q>2$: this is $\mathcal C_1$ ([def-weil-pbc-C1]). Since $r$ is a prime different from $\operatorname{char}k$, $r$ is prime to $\operatorname{char}k$, so [lem-sc-c4] applies (with $\mathbf F_r$ constructible by step 1) and $H^q(C_{\Et},\mathbf F_r)$ is finite for all $q\ge0$: the conclusion of $\mathcal C_4$ ([def-weil-pbc-C4]), whose hypotheses (constructible, prime to $p$) hold by step 1. [lem-sc-c6] (same hypotheses, any algebraically closed $k'\supseteq k$) gives that $\rho^q_{k'/k}(C,\mathbf F_r)$ is an isomorphism for all $q$, which by step 2 is $\mathcal C_6$ ([def-weil-pbc-C6]; its hypothesis prime to $p$ holds by step 1). [lem-sc-c8] ($r$ prime, any open immersion $j:U\hookrightarrow C$) gives surjectivity of the restriction on $H^2$, which by step 2 is $\mathcal C_8$ ([def-weil-pbc-C8]). (Stacks 0A5B, Case I: $\ell\neq\operatorname{char}k$; vanishing and finiteness from 03RQ and 03RR, invariance from the invariance of $g$ and of the number of punctures, $\mathcal C_8$ because a proper open $U\subsetneq C$ is affine and has $H^2=0$.)

Part (a), conditional assertions ($r\neq\operatorname{char}k$). If $C$ is affine, it is a smooth affine connected curve (affine schemes are separated), so [lem-sc-c2] with $n=r$ prime gives $H^q(C_{\Et},\mathbf F_r)=0$ for $q>1$: $\mathcal C_2$ ([def-weil-pbc-C2]). If $C$ is proper, it is a smooth proper connected curve, and [lem-sc-c5] and [lem-sc-c7], which allow an arbitrary prime, in particular $r\neq\operatorname{char}k$, give finiteness of all $H^q(C_{\Et},\mathbf F_r)$ ($\mathbf F_r$ constructible by step 1) and bijectivity of all $\rho^q_{k'/k}(C,\mathbf F_r)$: by step 2 these are $\mathcal C_5$ ([def-weil-pbc-C5]) and $\mathcal C_7$ ([def-weil-pbc-C7]).

source.place: Lemma 0A5B (Tag 0A5B), proof, Case I: projective case 03RQ, affine case 03RR

proof.text: Part (b) ($\operatorname{char}k=p>0$, $r=p$). [lem-sc-c1] with $n=p$ (a prime) gives $\mathcal C_1$. [lem-sc-c3] ($\operatorname{char}k=p>0$, $C$ smooth separated connected) gives $H^q(C_{\Et},\mathbf F_p)=0$ for $q>1$, the conclusion of $\mathcal C_3$ ([def-weil-pbc-C3]), whose hypothesis ($\mathbf F_p$ is $p$-primary) holds by step 1. [lem-sc-c8] with $r=p$ gives $\mathcal C_8$ (via step 2). If $C$ is affine, [lem-sc-c2] with $n=p$ gives $\mathcal C_2$. If $C$ is proper, [lem-sc-c5] and [lem-sc-c7] with $r=p$ (both allow $r=\operatorname{char}k$) give $\mathcal C_5$ and, via step 2, $\mathcal C_7$. (Stacks 0A5B, Case II: vanishing by 0A3N, finiteness and invariance in the proper case by 0A3P.)

Part (a), $H^0$, the Kummer sequence and $H^2$ of an affine curve ($r\neq\operatorname{char}k$). Since $r$ is prime to $\operatorname{char}k$, [lem-sc-primitive-root] gives a primitive $r$-th root of unity $\zeta\in k$, and the trivialization $\theta_\zeta:\mathbf F_r\to\mu_r$, $a\mapsto\zeta^a$, of [def-sc-mu-trivialization] is an isomorphism of etale sheaves; applying the functors $H^q(C_{\Et},-)$ gives isomorphisms $H^q(C_{\Et},\mathbf F_r)\cong H^q(C_{\Et},\mu_r)$ for all $q$. As $C$ is a smooth separated connected curve, [lem-sc-brauer-zero] gives $H^2(C_{\Et},\mathbf G_m)=0$, which is the hypothesis of [lem-sc-kummer-les] (with $n=r$). That lemma gives, $C$ being connected, $H^0(C_{\Et},\mu_r)=\mu_r(k)\cong\mathbf Z/r\mathbf Z$, and, with $\operatorname{Pic}(C)$ identified with $H^1(C_{\Et},\mathbf G_m)$ by [lem-sc-h1-gm-pic], the short exact sequence $0\to\mathcal O_C(C)^\times/\mathcal O_C(C)^{\times r}\to H^1(C_{\Et},\mu_r)\to\operatorname{Pic}(C)[r]\to0$. Composing with $\theta_\zeta$ gives $H^0(C_{\Et},\mathbf F_r)\cong\mathbf Z/r\mathbf Z$ and the stated sequence for $H^1(C_{\Et},\mathbf F_r)$. If $C$ is affine, $H^2(C_{\Et},\mathbf F_r)=0$ is the case $q=2$ of $\mathcal C_2$ (step 4, [lem-sc-c2]).

source.place: Lemma 03PL (Tag 03PL, the Kummer sequence), Theorem 03RM (Tag 03RM, H^q(X,G_m)=0 for q>=2), Lemma 03RR (Tag 03RR, (1) and (3)), Lemma 03RQ (Tag 03RQ, (1))

proof.text: Part (a), proper case ($r\neq\operatorname{char}k$). If $C$ is proper, it is a smooth proper connected curve of genus $g$ ([def-sc-genus]) and $r\ge1$ is prime to $\operatorname{char}k$, so [thm-sc-proper-cohomology] with $n=r$ gives, under $\theta_\zeta$, $H^0(C_{\Et},\mathbf F_r)\cong\mathbf Z/r\mathbf Z$, $H^1(C_{\Et},\mathbf F_r)\cong(\mathbf Z/r\mathbf Z)^{2g}$, $H^2(C_{\Et},\mathbf F_r)\cong\mathbf Z/r\mathbf Z$ and $H^q(C_{\Et},\mathbf F_r)=0$ for $q>2$.

Part (a), field extension ($r\neq\operatorname{char}k$). Let $k\subseteq k'$ be algebraically closed. By step 3 ([lem-sc-c6] and step 2), $\rho^q_{k'/k}(C,\mathbf F_r)$ is an isomorphism for every $q\ge0$. By [lem-sc-primitive-root] the image $\zeta'$ of $\zeta$ in $k'$ is a primitive $r$-th root of unity and $\theta_\zeta$ is compatible with pullback along $k\subseteq k'$: the pullback of $\mu_r$ to $C_{k'}$ maps to $\mu_r$ on $C_{k'}$, the section $\zeta$ of $\mu_r$ pulls back to the section $\zeta'$, so $\pi_{k'}^{-1}\theta_\zeta=\theta_{\zeta'}$ on the constant sheaf $\pi_{k'}^{-1}\mathbf F_r=\underline{\mathbf Z/r\mathbf Z}$ (step 2). (Stacks 0A5B, Case I: invariance because the genus $g$ and the number of punctures do not change from $k$ to $k'$.)

Part (d). By steps 3 and 4 (case $r\neq\operatorname{char}k$) and step 5 (case $r=\operatorname{char}k$), every assertion whose hypotheses hold for $(C,\mathbf F_r)$ has been proved. The remaining ones hold vacuously: $\mathcal C_3$ in case (a) because its hypothesis requires $\operatorname{char}k=p>0$ and $\mathbf F_r$ $p$-primary, which fails by step 1; $\mathcal C_4$ and $\mathcal C_6$ in case (b) because $\mathbf F_p$ is not prime to $p$ (step 1); $\mathcal C_2$ when $C$ is not affine and $\mathcal C_5$, $\mathcal C_7$ when $C$ is not proper. Hence $\mathcal C(C,\mathbf F_r)$, the conjunction of [def-weil-pbc-eight-curve-assertions], holds.

split_report.summary: Split along Stacks Lemma 0A5B (Case I r != char k, Case II r = char k) into nine steps: coefficient conditions (pair, constructible, prime to p / p-primary; elementary), identification of the maps (c) (elementary), the clause groups (a) unconditional C1 C4 C6 C8, (a) conditional C2 C5 C7, (b) C1 C3 C8 C2 C5 C7, each a conjunction of lem-sc-c1..c8 with the hypotheses matched (r prime; r != char k is r prime to char k; affine implies separated; c5 and c7 allow any prime); the explicit groups from lem-sc-kummer-les + lem-sc-brauer-zero + theta_zeta (any smooth connected C, so the Kummer sequence and H^0 hold beyond the affine case) and thm-sc-proper-cohomology; field-extension compatibility from lem-sc-c6 + lem-sc-primitive-root; and a new clause (d), the full conjunction C(C,F_r) with the vacuous assertions, which is how prop-weil-pbc-algebraically-closed-extension uses the node. Statement made precise: r prime (all cited c-lemmas but c4 and c6 need it), F_r constructible and torsion, C_j read as implications for the single pair, the vague 'all identifications compatible with field extension' replaced by the pullback isomorphisms and the compatibility of theta_zeta. thm-sc-affine-cohomology (unit sk-prop-cd-affine) and thm-sc-constant-invariance (sk-prop-ext-invariance) are no longer used: their units are not cited by sk-thm-p1, and the route nodes above cover what they gave. Proof now follows Stacks (proof_origin document). Mathlib: no etale cohomology of curves; no leaf.
